Ratios and proportions: A ratio compares two quantities, written a : b or a / b. A proportion says two ratios are equal, a / b = c / d, and it can be solved by cross multiplication: a x d = b x c. Rates compare quantities with different units. A ratio like 2 : 3 can be used to share a total: the parts are 2 and 3 out of 5. Scale drawings use a proportion between a drawing length and the real length.
Similar polygons: Two polygons are similar if their corresponding angles are congruent and their corresponding sides are proportional. The common ratio of the sides is the scale factor. If the scale factor is k, then the perimeters are in the ratio k and the areas are in the ratio k squared. Similar figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size.
Triangle similarity AA, SSS, SAS: Triangles are similar if two angles of one are congruent to two angles of the other (AA), if all three pairs of sides are proportional (SSS similarity), or if two pairs of sides are proportional and the included angles are congruent (SAS similarity). Similar triangles are useful for indirect measurement such as finding the height of a tree from shadows.
Midsegment and side-splitter theorems: A midsegment of a triangle joins the midpoints of two sides. The Triangle Midsegment Theorem says it is parallel to the third side and half as long. The Side-Splitter (Triangle Proportionality) Theorem says that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally. The converse is also true: if a line divides two sides proportionally, it is parallel to the third side.
